note: Below Dale Hollow Dam on the Obey River, beside the national fish hatchery, with trout fishing in the river and a fishing pier. There is no lake access from the campground; the nearest ramp is at Pleasant Grove, 3 miles away. Most pads are gravel, about a dozen are paved RV-only sites, and site 37 has no hookups. The campground is low-lying and some sites pond in heavy rain. Gates are closed 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. --Claude
summary: USACE tailwater campground confirmed on recreation.gov: 73 single sites, $32, 50-amp + water (not 37), showers, laundry, dump, Wi-Fi; season 04-09 to 10-24; 2-night weekend / 3-night holiday minimum. rec.gov's 'Lakefront' tag on sites 43-60 re-audited - not waterfront kept. Phone empty -> 931-243-3554.
flags: WATERFRONT CONTRARY CLAIM (re-audited, kept not waterfront): recreation.gov tags sites 43, 45, 47, 48, 49, 51, 53, 54, 56, 58, 59, 60 'Proximity to Water: Lakefront' - that water is the Obey River tailwater (~60-70 m wide), not the lake. Site points sit ~20-35 m from the river (e.g. 49 at 36.53793,-85.45930; 53 at 36.53769,-85.45872; 58 at 36.53729,-85.45790), but imagery shows a continuous riparian tree/brush strip along the whole bank and every site photo shows the pad backed by dense woods with no water in view. No open apron, so not riverfront; no visible water, so not riverview. Bank height could not be read under canopy. The stored evidence's '60-100 m' distance overstates it; the treeline is the reason.
